answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to post a slashable bond and collect time-delayed attestations from already-staked peers. At dawn each cycle, unverified clones are cheap to spawn but expensive to keep, because a farm that mints hundreds of names still has to lock capital for each one. Reputation then behaves like a glacier: it advances only through slow, attested work, and a single jade seal from a high-stake neighbor is what finally grants the newcomer voting weight.
